name: Philippines
prevalence_note: BSP, CICC (1326), NTC & NBI 2025-2026: GCash/Maya wallet 'account upgrade' MPIN & OTP vishing in Tagalog and English, fake NBI arrest-warrant & unordered COD parcel extortion, fake NTC SIM deactivation calls, and online task commission deposit scams dominate.
cross_border_note: Scammers call in Tagalog, Taglish, and English using unregistered +63 SIMs, illegal SMS blaster/spoofing gear, and foreign VoIP numbers; victims can report scams to the CICC 1326 hotline.

scams.name: Bank, GCash & Maya Account Upgrade OTP Vishing
scams.name_en: Bank, GCash, or Maya credit-limit upgrade and OTP/MPIN vishing scam
scams.signals_en: Callers address the recipient by name while posing as Philippine bank fraud officers or GCash/Maya agents offering a limit upgrade, points conversion, or urgent account verification to capture OTPs, MPINs, or CVVs.
scams.legit_en: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), banks, GCash, and Maya remind consumers under AFASA that official staff never send clickable text links or ask for passwords, MPINs, CVVs, or OTPs.
bait_tactics: Hold on for a second, the electric fan right beside me is pretty loud so I missed that part, could you repeat which department you're calling from?
Wait a bit, I left my reading glasses in the bedroom so I can't read any small messages on my phone screen right now.
Our home internet has been super slow since this morning, could you spell out the reference code again while I look for a notepad?

scams.name: Pekeng GCash / Maya Account Upgrade at OTP o MPIN Scam
scams.name_en: Tagalog-language fake GCash, Maya, or bank caller stealing OTPs and MPINs
scams.signals_en: Caller in Tagalog/Taglish poses as GCash, Maya, or government ayuda staff claiming the user's e-wallet needs an urgent security upgrade or won a cash promo, pressuring them to dictate their MPIN, SMS OTP, or share their screen.
scams.legit_en: GCash, Maya, and BSP-regulated banks never phone users in Tagalog or English to ask for MPINs, OTP codes, or screen sharing.
bait_tactics: Sandali lang po ha, mahina ang signal dito sa loob ng bahay kaya wala pang pumapasok na text message sa akin.
Naiwan ko po iyong salamin ko sa kabilang kuwarto kaya hindi ko mabasa nang maayos ang screen, puwede bang ulitin ninyo nang dahan-dahan?
Wala naman po akong laman sa GCash ngayon kaya bukas na lang po ako magtatanong mismo sa help center sa loob ng app.

scams.name: Pekeng NBI Warrant, Pulis at Unordered COD Parcel Scam
scams.name_en: Tagalog fake NBI arrest-warrant, money-laundering, or unordered COD parcel extortion call
scams.signals_en: Caller in Tagalog poses as an NBI agent, police officer, or customs/courier representative alleging an arrest warrant, bounced-order complaint, or illegal parcel under the victim's name, demanding hush money or 'bail/settlement' sent via GCash or Maya.
scams.legit_en: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and Philippine courts serve subpoenas formally in writing and never demand GCash/Maya settlements over phone calls.
bait_tactics: Naku po, pupunta na lang po ako nang personal sa pinakamalapit na NBI clearance center bukas ng umaga kasama ang kapatid ko.
Maingay po kasi ang ulan sa bubong namin ngayon, puwede po bang sabihin ulit nang mabagal kung saang sangay kayo tumatawag?

scams.name: Fake NTC Telecommunications Regulator SIM Suspension Call
scams.name_en: Fake NTC regulator threatening immediate SIM deactivation unless clearance fee is paid
scams.signals_en: Callers impersonate National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) staff alleging the subscriber's registered SIM card was flagged for spam/scam activity and faces immediate deactivation unless a clearance fee is paid.
scams.legit_en: The NTC and Philippine mobile carriers never call individual subscribers to extort clearance fees or request banking credentials to prevent SIM deactivation.
bait_tactics: Oh really, let me think which ID card was used when this SIM was registered, could you repeat the division details slowly?
Give me a moment please, someone is knocking at the front gate for water delivery, go ahead and explain the notice again.

scams.name: Online Task and Commission Deposit Recruitment Scam
scams.name_en: Part-time online task and advance e-wallet deposit recruitment scam
scams.signals_en: Callers follow up on unsolicited Viber/Telegram/SMS job offers promising daily GCash/Maya payouts for liking videos or rating merchant items, then demand advance 'top-up deposits' to unlock frozen commissions.
scams.legit_en: Legitimate Philippine employers and e-commerce platforms never require applicants to deposit personal money to unlock wages or merchant orders.
bait_tactics: Wait, I'm not very familiar with how online merchant tasks work, could you walk me through your SEC registration details first?
Hold on a bit, my phone battery is almost drained and I can't find my charger cable, could you explain the payout rules again?
